n5-licao-jobs.titulo: The one-off job and the scheduled pickup: Job and CronJob
n5-licao-jobs.enunciado:
A Deployment is for what can’t stop (the store that stays open). For what needs to finish (generating a report, migrating the database, taking a backup), use a Job:

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: relatorio
spec:
  completions: 3      # must succeed 3 times
  parallelism: 2      # at most 2 at the same time
  backoffLimit: 6     # how many failures to accept before giving up
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never   # or OnFailure (never Always)
      containers:
      - name: relatorio
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh", "-c", "echo gerando relatorio"]

A pod that finishes well becomes Completed (the log is still there: kubectl logs job/relatorio). One that fails makes way for another, with a growing wait (10s, 20s, 40s...). Past the backoffLimit, the Job becomes Failed. To wait for the end in a script: kubectl wait --for=condition=complete job/relatorio.

CronJob: the Job with a set time

The CronJob creates a Job at each time in its schedule, in cron format: minute hour day month day-of-week.

  • */5 * * * *: every 5 minutes;
  • 0 3 * * *: every day at 3 a.m.;
  • 0 7 * * 2: every Tuesday at 7 a.m. (Sunday is 0).

To test without waiting for the time: kubectl create job teste --from=cronjob/NAME. The CronJob keeps the latest Jobs (3 that succeeded and 1 that failed, by default) and deletes the older ones.
n5-licao-jobs.vidaReal: The Job is a contract job: the bricklayer comes, does the work and leaves (if it goes wrong, he tries again). The CronJob is the garbage pickup: every Tuesday at 7 a.m., without anyone having to ask.
n5-licao-jobs.limite: The “try again” has a limit (backoffLimit) and waits longer and longer between attempts: an error in the command doesn’t fix itself.

n5-licao-daemonset-init.titulo: The fire extinguisher in every building and the inspection before the move
n5-licao-daemonset-init.enunciado:
DaemonSet: one pod on each node

Log collection, networking, monitoring: some things need to run on every node. The DaemonSet guarantees one pod per node, and puts the pod on every new node by itself. The cluster itself uses it: see kubectl get ds -n kube-system (kube-proxy and the kindnet network).

There are no replicas: the number of nodes is what counts. To pick the nodes, use nodeSelector; to get onto a node with a taint (like the control plane), use tolerations.

Init container: before everything else

The initContainers run before the app’s containers, in order, and each one must finish successfully. Good for preparing files, waiting for a database, migrating data. Meanwhile, the pod shows Init:0/1; if one fails, Init:Error or Init:CrashLoopBackOff.

Sidecar: alongside, from start to finish

An init container with restartPolicy: Always becomes a sidecar: it starts before the app, keeps running next to it (shipping logs, acting as a proxy) and exits when the app finishes. In a Job this matters: a regular container that never finishes leaves the Job stuck forever.
n5-licao-daemonset-init.vidaReal: The DaemonSet is the condo rule: every building has a fire extinguisher, including the one that’s finished tomorrow. The init container is the inspection: the move only comes in after it’s done. The sidecar is the assistant who works alongside the resident.
n5-licao-daemonset-init.limite: The extinguisher only goes to the buildings that accept it: the management office (the control plane) has a taint, and the DaemonSet only gets in there with the toleration.

n5-primeiro-job.enunciado: Create the Job boas-vindas (image busybox:1.36) that writes obra concluída (“work done”) to the log and finishes.
n5-primeiro-job.dica: command: ["sh", "-c", "echo obra concluída"], and restartPolicy Never or OnFailure.
n5-primeiro-job.vidaReal: Calling the bricklayer for a single job: he does it and leaves.
n5-primeiro-job.limite: The bricklayer leaves, but the receipt (the Completed pod and the log) stays until someone throws it away.
n5-primeiro-job.comoSaber: kubectl get jobs shows Complete; kubectl logs job/boas-vindas shows the phrase.

n5-politica.enunciado: This Job is rejected when you apply it. Read the error and fix it (the work itself is right).
n5-politica.dica: A Job accepts restartPolicy OnFailure or Never. Always is for what can’t stop (Deployment).
n5-politica.vidaReal: The contract says “when you finish, start over”: that’s not a contract job, it’s a permanent position.
n5-politica.limite: Kubernetes rejects the contract right at the door: it doesn’t even create the Job.

testes.descricao: the Job is accepted and finishes

n5-mutirao.enunciado: The Job paredes (walls) needs to finish 6 times, and each wall takes about 10 seconds. As it is, it builds one at a time. Adjust it to build 3 at the same time: the test waits 40 seconds at most.
n5-mutirao.dica: spec.completions (how many times) and spec.parallelism (how many at the same time).
n5-mutirao.vidaReal: Six walls to put up and only one bricklayer: it works, but it takes a while. With three bricklayers at the same time, it’s done in two rounds.
n5-mutirao.limite: More bricklayers only help if there’s room on the site: with no free CPU on the nodes, the extra pods wait (Pending).
n5-mutirao.comoSaber: kubectl get pods -l job-name=paredes -w: three pods at a time.

testes.descricao: the 6 walls are done within 40 seconds

msgs.1: at least 3 bricklayers at the same time
msgs.2: the Job paredes finished successfully 6 times

n5-erro-de-digitacao.enunciado: The Job migracao is failing. Find out why in the logs (kubectl logs job/migracao) and fix the file. Hint: a Job can’t change its command; delete it and create it again (kubectl delete job migracao and apply).
n5-erro-de-digitacao.dica: The log says “sh: exti: not found”: the command has a typo.
n5-erro-de-digitacao.vidaReal: The bricklayer tries, fails, comes back later, fails again: the blueprint has a mistake and he has no way of guessing it.
n5-erro-de-digitacao.limite: Kubernetes doesn’t read the log: it only sees that the command exited with an error (a code other than 0) and tries again.

testes.descricao: the safety locks are still there

msgs.0: the migration is still in the command (the log says “migrando o banco”): swapping the work for exit 0 migrates nothing

n5-coleta.enunciado: Create the CronJob limpeza (cleanup) that runs every 5 minutes (the work is already in the file).
n5-coleta.dica: The schedule in cron format: minute hour day month day-of-week. “Every 5” is */5.
n5-coleta.vidaReal: The pickup comes every 5 minutes, on its own, without anyone calling to ask for it.
n5-coleta.limite: The truck leaves on time even if the previous pickup hasn’t finished yet (unless the rule says Forbid).
n5-coleta.comoSaber: kubectl get cronjob shows the schedule; after 5 minutes, kubectl get jobs shows the first Job.

testes.descricao: the pickup comes on its own

msgs.0: a Job from limpeza ran and finished

n5-coleta-agora.enunciado: The CronJob backup runs every day at 3 a.m. Run it now, by creating a Job named teste from it, and tell how many files the backup copied (it’s in the log).
n5-coleta-agora.dica: kubectl create job teste --from=cronjob/backup; then kubectl logs job/teste.
n5-coleta-agora.vidaReal: The backup runs at 3 in the morning. Nobody is going to stay up to see if it works: you ask for an extra run now.
n5-coleta-agora.limite: The extra run counts as a regular Job: it doesn’t change the CronJob’s schedule.

n5-extintor.titulo: A fire extinguisher in every building
n5-extintor.enunciado: Create the DaemonSet extintor (the extinguisher; image busybox:1.36, command sleep infinity), so there’s one pod on each worker node. The hidden tests will build a new building.
n5-extintor.dica: It looks like a Deployment without replicas: kind DaemonSet, selector, template.
n5-extintor.vidaReal: Every building has a fire extinguisher, including the one the builder hands over next week.
n5-extintor.limite: A closed-off building (with a taint) doesn’t get the extinguisher without a toleration.
n5-extintor.comoSaber: kubectl get ds shows DESIRED 2; kubectl get pods -o wide, one pod on node-1 and another on node-2.

testes.descricao: one extinguisher on each worker node
the new building gets the extinguisher too

n5-extintor-na-administracao.titulo: An extinguisher in the management office too
n5-extintor-na-administracao.enunciado:
The DaemonSet extintor is on node-1 and node-2, but not on control-plane. Find out why (kubectl describe node control-plane, under Taints) and get the extinguisher there too.

A taint is a sign on the building that keeps pods away. To get in anyway, the pod carries a toleration with the sign’s key and effect, in spec.template.spec.tolerations (next to containers). You’ll see both in depth in level 7.

tolerations:
- key: KEY            # the taint’s key
  operator: Exists    # any value works
  effect: EFFECT      # the taint’s effect
n5-extintor-na-administracao.dica: A toleration for the key node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, effect NoSchedule (operator Exists).
n5-extintor-na-administracao.vidaReal: The condo’s management office is a building with a “staff only” sign. The extinguisher gets in if it’s authorized.
n5-extintor-na-administracao.limite: The toleration allows entry, it doesn’t force it: in a Deployment, the pod might or might not go to the management office.

testes.descricao: one extinguisher on each of the 3 nodes

n5-vistoria.enunciado: The painel (dashboard) only opens if the file /config/pronto exists, and the one that creates the file is the preparo (prep) container. Both start together, and the dashboard crashes (see kubectl logs painel -c painel). Make preparo run before and finish first, without the dashboard restarting.
n5-vistoria.dica: Move preparo from containers to initContainers (at the same level). A pod can’t change after it’s created: kubectl delete pod painel and apply.
n5-vistoria.vidaReal: The move and the inspection arrived together: the truck unloads before the inspection gives the OK, and everything goes back onto the truck.
n5-vistoria.limite: The inspection (init) runs once, when the pod starts; if the app restarts later, it doesn’t run again.
n5-vistoria.comoSaber: kubectl get pod painel goes through Init:0/1 and reaches 1/1 Running with 0 restarts.

testes.descricao: the dashboard opens on the first try

n5-sidecar.enunciado: The Job medicao has two containers: medicao (the measurement), which finishes in seconds, and enviador (the sender), which sends the report nonstop. Because of it, the Job never becomes Complete. Turn enviador into a real sidecar.
n5-sidecar.dica: A sidecar is an init container with restartPolicy: Always. A Job can’t change its template: delete the Job and apply again.
n5-sidecar.vidaReal: The measuring is done, but the messenger carrying the report stays on the site forever, and the contract job is never marked as finished.
n5-sidecar.limite: The sidecar exits when the app finishes; if the app never finishes (a server), the sidecar stays too.
n5-sidecar.comoSaber: kubectl get jobs shows Complete; kubectl get pods, the pod Completed.

testes.descricao: the measurement finishes and so does the Job
